previous_disclosures.summary: On November 22, 2023, Broadcom completed the acquisition of VMware in a cash-and-stock transaction valued at approximately $86.3 billion, where VMware stockholders received $30.8 billion in cash and 54.4 million shares of Broadcom common stock.
Broadcom funded the cash portion of the VMware Merger consideration using $30.4 billion in term loans issued under a credit agreement dated August 15, 2023, along with cash on hand.

comparisons.peer_summary: NVIDIA employs a platform strategy combining hardware, systems, software, and services on a unified GPU-based architecture to serve diverse multi-billion-dollar end markets. The programmable nature of this architecture supports various software stacks developed internally or by third parties, and the large developer base strengthens the ecosystem and increases value to customers.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and NVDA utilize comprehensive platform strategies that integrate hardware with extensive software ecosystems to drive value. AVGO expanded its infrastructure software solutions through the VMware acquisition, stating this bolsters its capacity to address complex IT infrastructure issues. Similarly, NVIDIA employs a unified GPU-based architecture supported by internal and third-party software stacks, noting that its large developer base strengthens the ecosystem and increases platform value. While AVGO's recent strategic move involved acquiring an existing software entity (VMware) to broaden its software portfolio, NVIDIA's approach focuses on building a programmable architecture with integrated software tools (like CUDA) to serve diverse markets.

sentences.text: On November 22, 2023, we acquired VMware in a cash-and-stock transaction (the "VMware Merger"), in which VMware stockholders received, in aggregate, approximately $30.8 billion in cash and 544 million shares of Broadcom common stock (on a split adjusted basis) with a fair value of $53.4 billion.
With the VMware Merger, we have bolstered our infrastructure software solutions and are able to offer our customers a greater capacity to address complex IT infrastructure issues.
NVIDIA has a platform strategy, bringing together hardware, systems, software, algorithms, libraries, and services to create unique value for the markets we serve.

The programmable nature of our architecture allows us to support several multi-billion-dollar end markets with the same underlying technology by using a variety of software stacks developed either internally or by third-party developers and partners.
The large and growing number of developers and installed base across our platforms strengthens our ecosystem and increases the value of our platform to our customers.
